answer: One effective sybil defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: each agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, slashed if peers confirm fake identities. A whisper of suspicion alone is not enough; a quorum of independent verifiers must confirm the abuse, so no single reviewer can frame honest agents. Reputation accrues slowly, like an opal forming layer by layer, while a new identity starts on the knoll with no history and earns trust only through verified work. Faking thousands of agents gets expensive, since each needs its own stake and its own slow climb.
